analysis.title: Ford Motor Co. (F): Higher commodity and logistics costs push out EBIT improvement to 2028, 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: 3Q26 was a mixed report. Revenue ($49.5 bn), adjusted EBIT ($2.7 bn) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.49) were all above the Street (FactSet), but the midpoint of implied 4Q26 EBIT guidance is below the Street because of higher commodity costs.
Ford raised its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5-$11.0 bn from $10.0-$11.0 bn. The new midpoint of $10.75 bn compares with GS and the Street at about $10.6 bn.
Implied 4Q26 adjusted EBIT is about $2.1 bn at the midpoint, versus GS prior at $2.4 bn and the Street at $2.2 bn.

Ford expects commodities, memory and logistics to be a roughly $2 bn yoy headwind in 2027. Management expects roughly flat yoy EBIT in 2027, which implies about $10.75 bn versus the Street at about $11.25 bn and GS prior at $11.27 bn.

GS sees Ford executing well on structural and warranty cost reduction and on mix, but the underlying cost environment is incrementally challenging. Cost headwinds offset positives such as the Oakville F-Series ramp in 2027.
GS assumes flattish EBIT in 2027 and improvement in 2028, helped by the ramp of the Energy business and the UEV platform.
Software, services and parts (auto-adjacent businesses) were about 10% of total revenue in the quarter. Management expects their growth to offset macro headwinds at Ford Credit in 2027.
Ford Energy remains on track to bring the full 20 GWh of capacity online by the end of 2027. 2028 capacity is expected to be fully committed by 1Q27, with talks for 2029 and 2030 capacity underway.
The Ford Fathom electric pickup remains on track to launch in 4Q27, with pre-orders starting in 1Q27 at a starting price of $28,350.
Added Super Duty capacity at Oakville is expected to roughly offset planned production downtime for the next-gen F-150 in 2027.

Ford expects higher Model e investment in 2027 than in 2026 for the UEV platform, Ford Energy and European partnerships with Geely and Renault. The 2029 Model e breakeven target is unchanged, but progress will not be linear.
Wholesale units were 1,049k, 4.9% below GS at 1,103k and down 9.3% yoy. Ford Pro units (358k) missed GS by 8.6%, while Model e units (34k) beat GS by 13.3%.

GS cut its 12-month price target to $12 from $14, based on 6X (from 7X, reflecting peer multiples) normalized EPS of $1.95 (from $2.05). Rating stays Neutral, reflecting a muted volume environment and a premium multiple relative to peers.
GS EPS estimates for CY26/27/28 are now $1.90/$1.85/$2.00 versus $1.87/$2.00/$2.10 prior. 2026 is higher on the 3Q upside, and 2027/2028 are lower on higher costs.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $12 from $14 on a 6X multiple (from 7X) applied to normalized EPS of $1.95. Rating stays Neutral on muted volumes and a premium multiple versus peers, with about 0.4% upside to the $11.95 price.

sector_views.rationale: US market is at relatively normalized levels, competition is challenging in international markets, and commodity, logistics and memory costs are rising.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $49.5 bn versus GS est $51.1 bn and Street (FactSet) est $49.1 bn. Revenue was down 3.1% versus GS and up 0.9% versus the Street.
3Q26 reported adjusted EBIT $2.7 bn (5.4% of sales) versus GS est $2.3 bn (4.4%) and Street est $2.4 bn (5.0%).
3Q26 reported non-GAAP operating EPS $0.49 versus GS est $0.38 and Street est $0.41. Adjusted FCF was $4.7 bn in the quarter.

Ford attributed the yoy EBIT increase to better volume and mix (~$0.2 bn), pricing (~$0.1 bn), and lower regulatory expenses plus higher software and services contributions (~$0.4 bn), partly offset by ~$0.7 bn of higher costs.

Segment EBIT in 3Q26 (reported): Ford Blue $1,392 mn versus GS est $985 mn, Model e -$1,058 mn versus GS est -$1,048 mn, Ford Pro $1,665 mn versus GS est $1,871 mn, Ford Credit EBT $803 mn versus GS est $592 mn.

2026 guidance (company): adjusted EBIT $10.5-$11.0 bn (from $10.0-$11.0 bn), Ford Blue ~$5.5 bn, Ford Pro ~$7.0 bn (from $7.0-$7.5 bn), Model e about -$4.0 bn (unchanged), Ford Credit EBT ~$2.8 bn (from >$2.5 bn). Adjusted FCF $6.0-$7.0 bn (unchanged) and capex $9.5-$10.5 bn (unchanged).
Commodity headwind for 2026 is now approaching ~$2.5 bn (from just above $2 bn prior). Guidance excludes a sustained Middle East conflict or a US economic downturn.
Implied 4Q26 adjusted EBIT guidance is $1.85-$2.35 bn, midpoint $2.1 bn, versus GS prior est $2.4 bn (-12.5%) and Street est $2.2 bn (-4.7%).
GS forecasts (estimates): EPS $1.90 in 2026, $1.85 in 2027 and $2.00 in 2028. Quarterly EPS est is $0.34 for 4Q26 (12/26E) and 1Q27 (3/27E), and $0.54 for 2Q27 (6/27E).

macro_indicators.indicator: US SAAR assumption in Ford guidance
macro_indicators.interpretation: Ford raised its assumption for total US auto sales pace, which supports its higher EBIT guidance floor.

macro_indicators.indicator: US industry pricing assumption in Ford guidance
macro_indicators.interpretation: Ford assumes slightly firmer vehicle pricing, partly offsetting commodity cost pressure.
Rising commodity costs are the main reason implied 4Q26 EBIT is below the Street.

macro_indicators.indicator: Commodities, memory and logistics headwind to Ford
macro_indicators.interpretation: This cost increase is why management expects roughly flat 2027 EBIT despite volume and mix gains.

risk_factors: Auto cycle: demand and price-mix could be weaker or stronger than GS expects.
Ford could gain or lose more market share than GS expects.
Non-auto markets such as Defense and Energy.
A larger or smaller tariff impact than expected.
Margin and pricing pressure in a downturn, success of initiatives such as the transition to hybrids and EVs, and the ability to grow higher-margin software and services.
Guidance excludes a sustained Middle East conflict and a downturn in the US economy.
Rising commodity, memory and logistics costs, a ~$2 bn yoy headwind in 2027.
geopolitical: Ford's 2026 guidance does not include potential impacts from a sustained Middle East conflict.

tension_points.bull_case: Ford is reducing structural and warranty costs, improving mix, and growing high-margin software and physical services (about 10% of revenue). Oakville F-Series ramp, Ford Energy and the UEV platform support improvement in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Commodity, memory and logistics costs are a ~$2 bn yoy headwind in 2027, leaving EBIT roughly flat at ~$10.75 bn versus the Street at ~$11.25 bn. Volumes are muted and the multiple is at a premium to peers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Guidance excludes a sustained Middle East conflict or a US economic downturn, either of which would break the flat-2027 EBIT base case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher commodity, memory and logistics costs push out Ford's EBIT improvement to 2028 even as execution on structural costs and mix is good.
theme_stances.evidence: the underlying cost environment is incrementally challenging
